Israeli incursions and detentions spark nationwide protests

item.description:
Daily brief · 15 October 2026
Arrest of Baniyas massacre suspect Mihrac Ural sparks celebrations and calls for revenge
People's mood: Mostly neutral · The media: Mostly neutral
The dominant story is the arrest of Mihrac Ural (Ali Kayali), chief suspect in the 2013 Baniyas massacre, which triggered widespread celebrations among Syrians, especially in coastal and Sunni communities, alongside calls for his execution and skepticism about Turkish/Lebanese involvement claims. Netanyahu's disclosure of a secret call with al-Sharaa during the Suwayda violence sparked anger and accusations of Israeli electoral exploitation of Druze suffering, with Damascus firmly denying politicization. Continued Israeli incursions in Daraa and Quneitra, the Jibsa gas pipeline attack in Hasakah, coastal violence court verdicts, and routine economic/diplomatic news (investment pledges, currency crackdown, Aleppo-Moscow flights) round out the coverage, with public reaction ranging from religious gratitude and vindication to weary distrust of both outlet narratives and foreign actors.
